summary: George Island Light on Lake Winnipeg: a steel tower lit in 1906, keepers from 1906 to 1981, a 1930 drowning and a 1951 rescue by bush pilot. Seasonal today.

lens.note: Fixed white dioptric light of the seventh order as described in 1906; the current lens is not described in the sources

light.seasonal: Marked seasonal on the Coast Guard list

structures.type: open steel skeleton, red rectangular skeleton tower today
structures.note: 15.5 m is the Coast Guard's current figure. The 1906 report gives 64 ft (19.5 m) to the top of the ventilator. The sources do not reconcile the two.
Rectangular wooden building, 150 ft west of the tower
New keeper's dwelling built on the island

access.note: Island in the north basin of Lake Winnipeg. Lighthouse Friends says the modern light is best viewed by boat. No public landing arrangement or tour is described in the sources.

events.note: Tower built by day labour under the direction of M. J. Egan; steelwork built at the Sorel government shipyard
Established in the year ended 30 June 1906; the night of first lighting is not given
Fixed white dioptric light of the seventh order, 66 ft above the lake

Hand fog horn listed in the 1912 report's fog signal list. The keepers' tables mark George Island with an asterisk; the 1912 table's footnote reads '$25 for Fog Horn' (checked on the page image), the 1913 table's reads 'For blowing hand fog horn', and the 1915 table's reads '$25 for operating fog horn or bell'
Keeper Ingwald Thordarson lost after his rowboat drifted away; the boat was found bottom up and no bodies were recovered
Keeper Willard Olson stranded by an early freeze-up and taken off by a bush pilot on 7 December
Olson leaves the station and the light is automated. Lighthouse Friends also gives 1968 for electrification and automation in another passage.

keepers.name: A. A. T. McKay
keepers.note: Also A. A. Tashe McKay (Lighthouse Friends). Table gives appointment 6 Dec 1909 at George Island. The 1913 table lists him at Cox Reef. Lighthouse Friends gives 1909 to 1910.

keepers.name: John Thumser
keepers.note: Also J. Thumser (1913 table) and John Tumster (1912 footnote). The footnote dates his appointment 31 March 1910; the 1913 table gives Mar. 31, 1911.

keepers.name: E. Arrason
keepers.note: 1915 table gives appointment 26 Aug 1912 (OCR reads 'Aug. 2(), 1912'; corrected on the page image, scan 77). Lighthouse Friends gives service to 1924.

keepers.name: Ingwald Thordarson
keepers.note: Lost in October 1930 after an oar broke on his row back from the Wolverine; no bodies recovered (Lighthouse Friends).

keepers.name: W. L. Curran
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends gives 1931 to at least 1937.

keepers.name: Willard Olson
keepers.note: Longest serving keeper per Lighthouse Friends. Named only as that source prints him, in his public role.

wrecks.date: undated; reported in the year ended 30 June 1900
wrecks.outcome: Caught in a gale on Lake Winnipeg with a leak, towed by the steamer Lady of the Lake to Georges Island Harbour, grounded and still there; amount of loss not known

notes_for_editor: (1) The keeper names, dates and fog-horn footnotes from the Department tables were checked against the page images: Whiteway (scan 176, printed p. 169), McKay and Thumser (scan 256, printed p. 249: the George Island row, the footnote 'John Tumster, appointed to George Island 31st March 1910', and the '$25 for Fog Horn' note), Thumser and McKay at Cox Reef in 1913 (scan 80, printed p. 73), Arrason (scan 77: the image reads Aug. 26, 1912, where the OCR reads '2()'; the 1915 '$25 for operating fog horn or bell' note is on the same page). The 1912 fog-signal list page (scan 85, printed p. 78) was checked on its OCR page label only. (2) Conflicts left open in the story: Thumser's appointment is 31 Mar 1910 in the 1912 footnote and 31 Mar 1911 in the 1913 table; McKay's move from George Island to Cox Reef is not stated by the footnote; the tower height is 64 ft (19.5 m) in 1906 and 15.5 m today; automation is 1968 in one Lighthouse Friends passage and 1981 in another. (3) Lighthouse Friends is the only source for 1930 to 1981 and for the 1937 to 1951 gap is unfilled. The Star-Phoenix and Leader-Post articles it cites were not read directly. Newspaper search was not run: Chronicling America is a US archive. (4) Name collision: the Marine reports also list a 'George Island Light and Fog Bell' in Nova Scotia (Halifax harbour, Georges Island). None of those entries are used here. (5) 'Georges Island Harbour' (1900 wreck) is the report's wording; the report does not say it is the harbour near this light. (6) The record's Fl W 4s is replaced by the Coast Guard list's Fl W 5s; Wikipedia's 4 s was not used as a source. (7) Franklin Johnson, the teenage companion in 1930, is not named. (8) No photos proposed. (9) Lighthouse Friends' 'Olson' and 'Thordarson' details are used as that site prints them, with no further personal detail.
